courses.title: Engineering Statistics
courses.institution: HKUST, Department of Industrial Engineering and Decision Analytics
courses.summary: Graduate-level statistical methodology for data-driven engineering.
courses.overview: This course develops a rigorous statistical toolkit for engineering data analytics, covering probability foundations, random-sample theory, estimation and inference, regression modeling, regularization, generalized linear models, and modern classification methods.
courses.audience: Graduate students in engineering and data analytics, and advanced undergraduates with strong quantitative backgrounds.
courses.prerequisites: Probability theory, linear algebra, calculus, and basic programming/statistical computing.
outcomes: Formulate statistical inference problems and interpret assumptions in engineering contexts.
Construct and evaluate point estimators, hypothesis tests, and confidence sets.
Build and diagnose linear and generalized linear regression models.
Apply model selection, regularization, and cross-validation for predictive performance.
Compare and deploy classification methods based on data characteristics and evaluation metrics.

modules.title: Review of Probability Theory
modules.description: Events, conditional probability, random variables, expectation, transformations, and multivariate distributions as the foundation for inference.

modules.title: Properties of a Random Sample
modules.description: Sampling distributions, moment generating functions, order statistics, LLN/CLT, and delta-method approximations.

modules.title: Principles of Data Reduction
modules.description: Sufficient, minimal sufficient, and complete statistics, with factorization and exponential-family perspectives.

modules.title: Point Estimation
modules.description: Method of moments, maximum likelihood, Fisher information, Cramer-Rao bounds, and unbiased estimation under sufficiency/completeness.

modules.title: Hypothesis Testing
modules.description: Test construction, simple and composite hypotheses, UMP tests, likelihood-ratio methods, and sequential testing principles.

modules.title: Confidence Set
modules.description: Confidence-set construction via pivotal quantities and test inversion, plus asymptotic, bootstrap, and Bayesian intervals.

modules.title: Regression Models
modules.description: Multiple linear regression, least squares theory, inference, nested model tests, diagnostics, Box-Cox transforms, spline, and robust methods.

modules.title: Model Selection and Regularization
modules.description: Subset selection, ridge and lasso shrinkage, model criteria (Adjusted R2/Cp/AIC/BIC), and cross-validation workflows.

modules.title: Generalized Linear Model
modules.description: Logistic and Poisson regression, exponential-family formulation, estimation algorithms, and GLM inference/testing.

modules.title: Classification Methods
modules.description: LDA/QDA, k-NN, tree-based ensembles, and SVM methods for supervised classification tasks.

courses.title: Statistics for Engineers
courses.institution: HKUST, Department of Industrial Engineering and Decision Analytics
courses.summary: Core statistics for engineers: uncertainty modeling, estimation, inference, and regression.
courses.overview: This course introduces statistical thinking for engineering systems: data description, probabilistic modeling, statistical estimation, uncertainty quantification, and evidence-based decisions.
outcomes: Summarize and visualize engineering data effectively.
Apply probability models to quantify uncertainty.
Construct point estimates and confidence intervals.
Run hypothesis tests and interpret p-values responsibly.
Build and interpret basic linear regression models.

modules.title: Course Introduction
modules.description: Course goals, data-driven engineering decisions, and the role of statistics in the IEDA curriculum.

modules.title: Sampling Foundations
modules.description: Population vs. sample, sampling bias, and how sampling design impacts inference quality.

modules.title: Descriptive Statistics
modules.description: Summary measures and visual diagnostics for understanding variation and central tendency.

modules.title: Probability Distributions
modules.description: Discrete and continuous distributions, random variables, and model assumptions used in practice.

modules.title: Random Samples
modules.description: Sampling distributions, law of large numbers intuition, and central limit theorem viewpoints.

modules.title: Point Estimation
modules.description: Estimators, bias, variance, MSE tradeoffs, and principles for good estimator construction.

modules.title: Confidence Intervals
modules.description: Interval construction, interpretation under repeated sampling, and common misuse patterns.

modules.title: Hypothesis Testing
modules.description: Null/alternative setup, type I/II errors, p-values, power, and practical test selection.

modules.title: Comparing Multiple Samples
modules.description: Inference with more than two groups, model assumptions, and interpretation of group differences.

modules.title: Linear Regression
modules.description: Model fitting, coefficient interpretation, diagnostics, and prediction in engineering contexts.

courses.title: Applied Probability, Statistics and Data Analytics
courses.summary: Applied probability and statistical methods for engineering management contexts.

courses.title: Real Analysis Notes
courses.summary: Real analysis notes written at Nanjing University, with an English translation and a companion blog post.
courses.overview: A set of real analysis notes originally written in Chinese at Nanjing University in 2011 and later translated into English, with context and commentary in a companion blog post.
outcomes: Understand the measure-theoretic foundations behind modern real analysis.
Connect key results across topology, measure, integration, and differentiation.
Use the notes as a structured reference for study and teaching.

modules.title: Companion Blog Post

modules.description: Original Chinese real analysis notes written in 2011.
